answer: DeepWalk does not truly build the full graph in the streaming setting. In the original algorithm, it assumes the graph is already available as a whole so it can generate random walks over the complete adjacency structure before training the skip-gram model. In a streaming or incremental setting, the usual adaptation is to maintain the graph data structure as edges/nodes arrive and update the random-walk corpus or embeddings incrementally, rather than reconstructing the entire graph from scratch each time. So if someone says DeepWalk is used in streaming, that is typically an extension or implementation choice, not a property of vanilla DeepWalk itself.
